sentences.text: Heard the learned counsel appearing for the parties.

3. On the basis of the complaint lodged by Smt. Shabana w/o of the petitioner herein on 27.05.2023,
Mangaluru Women Police had registered FIR in crime No.44/2023 against the petitioner and two others for the aforesaid offences.
In the complaint, it is averred that the marriage of the complainant was performed with the petitioner on 10.11.2022.
Within 8 days from the date of marriage, her gold jewelleries were taken by the accused persons.
It is alleged in the complaint that the accused persons were quarrelling with the complainant on petty issues.
In the month of April 2023, she had informed the petitioner that she was pregnant.
Petitioner allegedly informed her that he was not ready for the same during that point of time and he did not want the baby.

He had purchased some Mohammad Hussain vs State Of Karnataka on 16 August, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/69210955/
2 tablets and given to her and as a result, complainant had suffered miscarriage.

sentences.text: Even thereafter, the accused persons allegedly ill-treated the complainant.
On 26.05.2023 complainant had gone to the house of her husband and that time her in-laws abused her and pushed her outside the house.
When the complainant fell down, NC: 2023:KHC:28900 her husband allegedly assaulted her, pronounced triple talaq and also threatened with dire consequences.
Immediately complainant informed about the incident to one Sri. Imran, who is the relative of complainant, and thereafter, got admitted at Unity Hospital.
Her statement was recorded in the hospital on 27.05.2023 at about 5.30 p.m. and based on the same, FIR in crime No.44/2023 was registered.

Apprehending arrest in the said case,
the petitioner filed Crl.Misc.No.569/2023 before the Court of the III Additional District and Sessions Judge, D.K., Mangaluru, which was dismissed on 03.07.2023.

entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Under these circumstances,
the petitioner is before this Court.
4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has reiterated the grounds urged in the petition and submits that there is a delay in lodging the complaint.
He also submits that the offence punishable under Sections 313 would not get attracted against the petitioner and in respect of other offences the maximum punishment is three years imprisonment.
Accordingly, prays to allow the petition.

5. Per contra, learned counsel appearing for the defacto complainant had opposed the bail application and NC: 2023:KHC:28900 submits that custodial interrogation of the petitioner is required as there are serious allegations against him.
He submits that the offence under Section 313 is serious in nature and therefore, prays to dismiss the petition.
6. Complainant is the wife of the petitioner and their marriage was performed on 10.11.2022.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that it was second marriage to both of them.
The allegation against the accused persons is that after marriage they were ill-treating the complainant.

Insofar as the allegation for the offence punishable under Sections 313 of the IPC is concerned, the complainant has stated that after she informed the petitioner about her pregnancy, petitioner had told her that he was not ready to have a baby and thereafter, bought some tablets and gave it to her.
It is not stated in the compliant that the complainant was compelled or forced to consume the said tablets by the petitioner.
Therefore, a doubt arises as to whether Section 313 of IPC would prima facie get attracted as against the petitioner.
Insofar as the other offences are concerned, the maximum punishment is imprisonment for three years.
Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner has no NC: 2023:KHC:28900 criminal antecedents.
There is a delay in lodging the complaint.
Under these circumstances, I am of the view that the petitioner has made out a prima facie case for grant of anticipatory bail.
7. Accordingly the petition is allowed.

The respondent - Police or any other police in the State of Karnataka are directed to release the petitioner in the event of his arrest in Crime No.44/2023 registered by Mangalore Women Police Station for the offences punishable under Sections 498A, 313, 323, 504 and 506 of the IPC, Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and Section 4 of the Muslim Women (Protection of Rights on Marriage) Act,
2019, subject to the following conditions:
